anomalies.observed: Both ground pins on each isolated CAN transceiver are connected to the same GND net: U10.4 (GND1) and U10.5 (GND2), and likewise U11.4 (GND1) and U11.5 (GND2).
anomalies.expected: The transceivers' logic-side and bus-side grounds should remain separate to preserve the specified CAN galvanic isolation.

evidence.quote: each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: Tying the two sides' grounds together defeats the transceivers' galvanic isolation, allowing ground differences and ground-loop currents between the controller and CAN wiring.

parsed.summary: The CAN transceivers are specified as isolated, but their logic-side and bus-side ground pins are all tied to GND. This defeats the intended galvanic isolation.
